item.title: High-quality remote sensing reflectance products over China and US coast
item.description:
High-quality remote sensing reflectance products over China and US coast
Shuhui Zhao, Youlv Wu, Jingning Lv, Dan Zhao, Yan Zheng, and Lian Feng
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 7475–7498, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-7475-2026, 2026
We created a 20-year dataset tracking coastal water conditions in China and the United States using satellite images. By improving how the satellite data are processed in areas with complex atmospheric conditions and diverse water properties, we produced more reliable and complete observations. This helps researchers better monitor environmental changes and water quality along coasts that are often difficult to study.

item.title: HaNi-Crop: A Harmonized and Gridded Global Dataset of Crop-Specific Nitrogen Inputs from Nitrogen Fertilizer and Manure
item.description:
HaNi-Crop: A Harmonized and Gridded Global Dataset of Crop-Specific Nitrogen Inputs from Nitrogen Fertilizer and Manure
Wensu Hao, Hanqin Tian, Hao Shi, Xing Yu, Naiqing Pan, Shufen Pan, Francesco N. Tubiello, Wulahati Adalibieke, Martial Bernoux, Philippe Ciais, Federico Maggi, Kazuya Nishina, Aimable Uwizeye, and Feng Zhou
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-595,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
HaNi-Crop dataset presents a long-term global dataset of nitrogen inputs from synthetic fertilizers and animal manure for different crops from 1961 to 2023. Built by combining agricultural statistics with crop distribution information, the dataset reveals how nutrient use has changed over time and provides a valuable resource for improving food production, environmental protection, climate change, and more sustainable agricultural management.

item.title: Coastal Atmosphere & Sea Time Series (CoASTS) and Bio-Optical mapping of Marine optical Properties (BiOMaP): the hyperspectral absorption coefficients by optically significant constituents
item.description:
Jean-François Berthon, Giuseppe Zibordi
Earth System Science Data, vol. 18, issue 10, pp. 7499-7514
DOI: 10.5194/essd-18-7499-2026
The Coastal Atmosphere & Sea Time Series (CoASTS) and the Bio-Optical mapping of Marine optical Properties (BiOMaP) programs were conceived and implemented to assist ocean color applications with field measurements of apparent and inherent optical properties, as well as concentration of optically significant water constituents. The CoASTS program led to the creation of time-series of bio-optical measurements at the “Acqua Alta” Oceanographic Tower (AAOT) site in the northern Adriatic Sea continued from 1995 up to 2016. The BiOMaP program supported the collection of equivalent bio-optical measurements across European Seas from 2000 up to 2022. This work focusses on CoASTS and BiOMaP hyperspectral absorption coefficients of optically significant constituents as determined applying standardized instruments, community measurement methods, extended quality control schemes and consolidated processing. The work, which complements a previous one by Zibordi and Berthon (2024) centred on multi-spectral data, presents the CoASTS and BiOMaP hyperspectral absorption coefficients of pigmented and non-pigmented particles in the 400–750 nm interval, and colored dissolved organic matter in the 350–680 nm one, both with a 3 nm spectral resolution at 2 nm increment. The data are available at https://doi.org/10.1594/PANGAEA.993510 (Berthon and Zibordi 2026).
